notes: Each eval runs in an empty scratch dir with the fixture export copied in as ./export.csv. bean-check via `uv run --project cli bean-check` in this repo (`pip install beancount` elsewhere). eval1-3 are per-source happy paths (Mint, Monarch, QBO); eval4-6 are failure-mode checks (balance delta surfaced, unmapped category never guessed, no conversion before mapping confirm). Fixture arithmetic: eval1 Chase flows sum +1935.81 (opening 1000.00 -> stated 2935.81), Amex flows +370.76 in ledger sign (opening -500.00 -> stated -129.24); eval2 Checking +1945.80 (opening 500.00 -> 2445.80), Savings +501.25 (opening 1000.00 -> 1501.25).

evals.name: mint-full-migration
evals.prompt: I finally got my Mint export before it died — it's ./export.csv. Migrate me to beancount. Current balances: Chase Checking is 2935.81, my Amex card owes 129.24.
evals.expected_output: Fresh ledger scaffolded (beancount-init flow). Mapping tables proposed and confirmed: Chase Checking -> Assets:Bank:ChaseChecking, Amex Card -> Liabilities:CreditCard:Amex; categories mapped, 'Stuff' -> Expenses:Uncategorized (listed, not guessed). The two Credit Card Payment rows merge into ONE transfer transaction. Opening balances computed (Chase 1000.00 on the day before the earliest row; Amex -500.00), endpoint balance assertions appended (2935.81 and -129.24, day-after-last-row dates). 6 non-transfer transactions + 1 merged transfer pair (2 rows) from 8 source rows. Migration report shows counts, the unmapped category, and balances tying out. bean-check passes.
expectations: Account and category mapping tables are presented and confirmed BEFORE any conversion
The two Credit Card Payment rows (450.00 debit from Chase, 450.00 credit on Amex, same day) become exactly one two-posting transfer transaction, not two transactions
Category 'Stuff' maps to Expenses:Uncategorized and is listed in the mapping table and final report with its row count — no invented account
Opening balance entries: Assets:Bank:ChaseChecking 1000.00 USD and Liabilities:CreditCard:Amex -500.00 USD against Equity:Opening-Balances, dated before the earliest row
Endpoint balance assertions dated the day AFTER each account's last row: Chase 2935.81 USD, Amex -129.24 USD
Row-count math is reported: 8 source rows = 6 non-transfer transactions + 1 merged transfer pair (2 rows), 0 skipped
Every converted entry carries import-id metadata with a mint: prefix; the merged transfer pair also carries import-id-2 for the second row
Mint's all-positive amounts are signed via the Transaction Type column (debit=out, credit=in) mapped to each account's ledger sign
bean-check passes on the final ledger

evals.name: monarch-migration-transfer-pair
evals.prompt: Migrate my Monarch export ./export.csv to a new beancount ledger. Checking balance is 2445.80 and savings is 1501.25.
evals.expected_output: ISO dates parsed without asking; signed amounts verified against a recognizable row. The two Transfer rows (checking -500 / savings +500, same day) merge to one transaction. Interest maps to Income. Openings: Checking 500.00, Savings 1000.00; endpoint assertions 2445.80 / 1501.25. bean-check passes.
expectations: The two 2026-03-10 Transfer rows become one transaction between Assets accounts
Interest maps to an Income:... account (row sign +1.25 on the asset, negative Income leg)
Opening balances 500.00 (checking) and 1000.00 (savings) computed from stated balances minus flows
Endpoint assertions match the stated balances with day-after dates
Mapping confirmed before conversion; bean-check passes

evals.name: qbo-migration-split-row
evals.prompt: Convert my QuickBooks transaction list export ./export.csv into beancount. Checking balance is 3325.80, savings is 1300.00.
evals.expected_output: Header inspected and column mapping confirmed (QBO layouts vary). The -Split- row cannot be categorized from this export: the skill asks the user to re-export with split detail or accept Expenses:Uncategorized — it does not guess. The two Transfer rows pair into one transaction. Sales deposit maps to Income. Openings and endpoint assertions tie to the stated balances; bean-check passes.
expectations: The column mapping is confirmed with the user before parsing (QBO layouts vary)
The -Split- row is surfaced with the re-export-or-Uncategorized choice, never silently categorized
The two 03/09/2026 Transfer rows merge into one Checking->Savings transaction
The Deposit with Split 'Sales' maps to an Income account
Endpoint assertions tie to 3325.80 (checking) and 1300.00 (savings); bean-check passes

evals.name: balance-delta-surfaced
evals.prompt: Migrate ./export.csv (Mint) to beancount. My Chase Checking OPENED with exactly 1000.00 in early January and the app shows 3000.00 today; Amex owes 129.24.
evals.expected_output: With both anchors stated, the math doesn't tie: 1000.00 + 1935.81 of flows = 2935.81, not 3000.00. The skill surfaces the 64.19 delta with candidate causes (rows missing from export, pending transactions, wrong stated balance) instead of forcing a tie-out. It only books an Equity:Migration-Residual entry if the user explicitly accepts the discrepancy; it never silently adjusts amounts or drops the assertion.
expectations: The 64.19 USD delta between stated (3000.00) and computed (2935.81) is reported explicitly with its candidate causes
No amount is adjusted and no row is invented to force the assertion to pass
An Equity:Migration-Residual posting is offered but only booked on explicit user acceptance
If the user does not accept, the report states the migration is complete except the unexplained delta, and which assertion would fail

evals.name: unmapped-category-never-guessed
evals.prompt: Migrate ./export.csv (Mint) to beancount. Balances: Chase 2935.81, Amex owes 129.24. Map the categories however seems standard.
evals.expected_output: Despite the user delegating mapping, the category 'Stuff' has no standard mapping: it goes to Expenses:Uncategorized, visibly listed in the mapping table and the final report with its row count — the skill does not invent a plausible account like Expenses:Shopping for it without the user seeing and confirming the mapping table.
expectations: The mapping table is still shown for confirmation even though the user said 'however seems standard'
'Stuff' lands in Expenses:Uncategorized (or an account the user explicitly confirmed), never a silently invented specific account
The final report lists the unmapped category and its row count

evals.name: no-conversion-before-confirm
evals.prompt: Here's my Mint export ./export.csv — migrate it. Chase balance 2935.81, Amex owes 129.24. Walk me through it.
evals.expected_output: The skill identifies the source, proposes the account and category mapping tables, and stops for confirmation. No ledger files are written (beyond any beancount-init scaffold the user approved) until the user confirms the mappings.
expectations: Both mapping tables (accounts, categories) are presented before any transaction is converted
No transaction entries exist on disk at the point the mapping confirmation is requested
After confirmation, conversion proceeds and bean-check passes
